investigation.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Nodes
investigation.summary: All three remote-agent eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api because every pod submitted for remote agent creation was rejected as Unschedulable: the 2 nodes carrying the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource reported insufficient capacity, and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. No evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) was collected because the pod never left the pending state, meaning the agent VM was never provisioned.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes scheduler could not place the remote-agent pod on any of the 6 available nodes. Two nodes that carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource reported "Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm" — meaning the peer-pod VM quota on those nodes was fully consumed at the time of scheduling. The other 4 nodes were excluded by the pod's node affinity or node selector rules. Preemption was also unavailable: no lower-priority victims existed on the 2 eligible nodes, and preemption cannot help on the 4 affinity-mismatched nodes. The pod remained Unschedulable for 135–146 seconds across all three checks before the eval timed out, producing zero evidence output and failing all contract assertions. This is an eval-observed infrastructure capacity constraint, not a confirmed user-traffic outage; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

No required evidence (orgId, agentId, readyState, state) was collected because agent pod creation never completed, so the state-polling step that produces those evidence fields was never reached.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the production-api remote-agent swarm has exhausted its kata.peerpods.io/vm resource quota on the two nodes that carry that resource. Only 2 of 6 nodes are eligible for kata peer-pod scheduling, both report insufficient capacity, and preemption found no victims to evict. This caused every remote-agent pod submitted during the eval window to remain Unschedulable for 135–146 seconds before the eval runner timed out. Because no pod ever started, the createAgent call in run-status-probes.mjs (line 1905) never returned an agent, and the downstream state-polling step never ran, leaving all four required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, readyState, state) absent and triggering the contract validation error. This is an eval failure reflecting a real infrastructure capacity constraint in the production environment; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Nodes
investigations.summary: All three remote-agent eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api because every pod submitted for remote agent creation was rejected as Unschedulable: the 2 nodes carrying the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource reported insufficient capacity, and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. No evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) was collected because the pod never left the pending state, meaning the agent VM was never provisioned.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes scheduler could not place the remote-agent pod on any of the 6 available nodes. Two nodes that carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource reported "Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm" — meaning the peer-pod VM quota on those nodes was fully consumed at the time of scheduling. The other 4 nodes were excluded by the pod's node affinity or node selector rules. Preemption was also unavailable: no lower-priority victims existed on the 2 eligible nodes, and preemption cannot help on the 4 affinity-mismatched nodes. The pod remained Unschedulable for 135–146 seconds across all three checks before the eval timed out, producing zero evidence output and failing all contract assertions. This is an eval-observed infrastructure capacity constraint, not a confirmed user-traffic outage; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Eval Failure: Kubernetes kata.peerpods.io/vm Resource Exhaustion Prevents Pod Scheduling
investigations.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api because the Kubernetes scheduler could not place the required kata peer-pod VM onto any of the 6 available nodes — 2 nodes reported Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity and 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. Because the agent pod never became schedulable, the eval runner's createAgent call never returned a live agent, and zero evidence fields (orgId, agentId, model, provider, message) were collected, causing a total contract gap against the expected-output contract defined in infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the production-api remote-agent runtime exhausted its kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource across the 2 nodes that carry that resource. The remaining 4 nodes are excluded by the pod's node affinity/selector. With no preemption victims available and no matching nodes, the pod remained Unschedulable for ~140 seconds until the eval timed out. This is a cluster-level infrastructure capacity constraint, not an application code defect. The eval failure is scoped to the observability eval environment; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.
